transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-02
Time: 09:30 PT / 12:30 ET
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jon Ramos (Redwood PM), Ravi Kumar (BlueHaven Cloud Architect), Sophie Lang (BlueHaven Head of Partnerships), Ethan Park (DevOps), Marta Silva (Security Lead)
Shared links: https://redwood.ai/partners/bluehaven-sync-deck (deck), https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/bh-sample-results-202703 (benchmarks spreadsheet)

Summary (auto-generated): Align refarch and marketplace listing steps; identify blockers for on-prem connector POC and security review.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Avery Chen: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we have about 50 minutes on this sync, um just high level we want to align on the marketplace packaging and the hybrid reference architecture for your on-prem plus hosted footprint.
[00:21] Sophie Lang: yeah thanks avery, appreciate you fitting this in, we want to make sure the listing doesn't force customers to move everything to the cloud, so the hybrid story is critical.
[00:34] Maya Patel: totally, and we have some patterns we've used with other partners, happy to walk through a couple of options, including dedicated capacity behind a VPC and an on-prem connector for KV cache and data in flight encryption.
[00:48] Ravi Kumar: quick context — we're running a mixture of cloud and colocation, main constraint is that PII payloads must not leave our EU region. Also our security team insists on customer-managed keys for any persisted traces.
[01:05] Marta Silva: yep that's right. we need KMS control, and audit logs for all inference requests. SOC2 is table stakes.
[01:12] Jon Ramos: just to set expectations from our side, marketplace listing can surface both hosted and dedicated offerings; private/on-prem connectors often listed as an add-on. the refarch we produce will show the recommended network flows and required IAM bits.
[01:28] Ethan Park: two quick practicals: one, can the on-prem connector run in air-gapped environments? second, how much open inbound on our firewall is needed for the connector?
[01:40] Maya Patel: good q — we have two connector patterns. pattern a is outbound-only egress to a regional relay (no inbound ports), pattern b supports a direct site-to-site VPN with mutual TLS for lower latency but requires peering config. air-gapped is tricky; we can offer an appliance packaging that ships as a container image with offline install steps.
[02:03] Ravi Kumar: okay outbound-only egress would be ideal. what about token/key rotation when customer-managed KMS is used?
[02:12] Maya Patel: token lifecycle is integrated with Redwood's private control plane; we can support bring-your-own-keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google KMS, and some HSM customers). key rotation flows can be automated, we can surface webhook callbacks for your key management ops. some words get fuzzy in transcripts, but the core is we don't store plaintext keys.
[02:36] Sophie Lang: and for marketplace listing, we want a single tile that advertises both hosted and hybrid; is that supported?
[02:44] Avery Chen: yes, you can have multiple SKUs under a listing. typically partners list: self-serve hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and an "on-prem connector" add-on. pricing and SLAs differ per SKU.
[02:57] Marta Silva: SLA for the connector itself — we need to know the failure modes and fallbacks. what if the regional relay is down?
[03:07] Maya Patel: good callout — we recommend multi-regional relay endpoints and automatic failover. fallback policy can also route requests to a compatible smaller model hosted in a fallback region with a notice flag so the app can handle degraded quality.
[03:22] Ravi Kumar: latency numbers? for typical seq len 1024 tokens, what are we looking at over the VPN vs relay?
[03:30] Maya Patel: ballpark, relay egress path will add about 60-120ms depending on region and network; site-to-site VPN can drop that to 30-60ms for well-peered networks. we should run microbenchmarks on your payloads — numbers change a lot with batch sizes.
[03:47] Ethan Park: yeah we have bursts at start of day, like 4k concurrent requests for short windows, so batch and autoscale behavior matters a lot. can dedicated pools handle that?
[03:58] Jon Ramos: dedicated pools are designed for predictable throughput; you configure reserved capacity and burst policies. autoscaling has limits tied to reserved vs burst quota, we can show how RU (request units) map to gpus.
[04:12] Sophie Lang: anything we need to include in the marketplace submission around networking? we've seen rejections for vague network diagrams.
[04:20] Avery Chen: include explicit VPC peering steps, required CIDR ranges, egress IP list, and KMS integration notes. we'll provide a trimmed checklist you can paste in the listing docs.
[04:33] Ethan Park: on the HSM side, will Redwood talk to our HSM directly or via cloud KMS?
[04:39] Maya Patel: depends — customers with on-prem HSMs usually use a gateway that Redwood can reach via mutual TLS and token broker, otherwise you can mirror keys into a cloud KMS under your control. both options supported but the appliance path is more involved.
[04:55] Marta Silva: for compliance we'll need a data flow diagram that highlights where PII is stripped, what is encrypted, and retention windows. can you produce that?
[05:03] Maya Patel: yes, we'll produce an annotated data flow that shows ingress, transformation, KV cache behavior, and retention TTLs.
[05:12] [09:05] Ravi Kumar: small note, our legal team also asked about reverse-SAML for partner portal access, any docs?
[05:19] Avery Chen: we have SAML/SSO guides for partners and marketplace portals, i'll share the integration guide link after the call.
[05:27] [09:40] Sophie Lang: switching gears, the refarch — can you sketch two options quickly? one minimal with relay-only; one full with site-to-site + dedicated?
[05:37] Maya Patel: sure — option one: hosted primary + relay-only connector. apps call the hosted API; PII is redacted client-side, connector handles encryption in transit, KV caching mostly on customer side. option two: dedicated reserved pool in your preferred region with site-to-site VPN to on-prem connector; KV cache co-located to avoid egress, lower latency, and better throughput. each option has different cost and ops tradeoffs.
[06:04] Ethan Park: curious on KV cache size and eviction semantics; our sessions can hit >50k tokens in some flows.
[06:12] Maya Patel: our KV cache supports segmented caches per-tenant and TTL-based eviction; for extremely long contexts we recommend explicit chunking and cache pinning in dedicated mode to avoid cold starts. we can share cache sizing heuristics.
[06:29] Ravi Kumar: OK. for the POC, we'd like Redwood to run a throughput pass with our sample payloads and the largest model we plan to use. can that be done in a test harness?
[06:39] Maya Patel: yes we can run microbenchmarks — we'll need your payloads, preferred models, and target p95 latency. we'll run tests in dev region and share results.
[06:49] Sophie Lang: any blockers we should anticipate for marketplace certification?
[06:53] Avery Chen: common blockers are missing network docs, unclear billing mapping for add-ons, and incomplete security artifacts. if we tick those off early it's smoother.
[07:05] Marta Silva: on security artifacts, can you confirm what you need for SOC2 scope mapping? logs, control descriptions, encryption attestations?
[07:14] Maya Patel: yes — we can provide SOC2 report, architecture control mappings, encryption in transit/at-rest descriptions, KMS integration notes, and sample audit log extracts. some parts may require an NDA for redacted logs.
[07:30] Ravi Kumar: good. also about billing — we want marketplace to support metered billing for hosted and committed for dedicated, is that supported?
[07:38] Avery Chen: marketplace supports multiple billing types; we can map SKUs to metered and committed plans. there's a standard billing connector we'll detail.
[07:46] Ethan Park: how do rollbacks work on model rollouts — we have to avoid regressions mid-release.
[07:52] Jon Ramos: Redwood has rollout primitives: canary, percentage traffic, and automatic fallback. rollouts tie to model versions and you can pin routes to specific versions. we also integrate with evals to detect quality regressions.
[08:08] Sophie Lang: about telemetry — what level of tracing will we see in console for a partnership account?
[08:13] Maya Patel: per-request traces, latency breakdown, token-level cost. for partners we can extend dashboards and give read-only views for partners or customers depending on permissions.
[08:24] [08:55] Ravi Kumar: last quick question — do you have any reference customers with a similar hybrid setup?
[08:30] Maya Patel: yes a healthcare partner in eu had a similar pattern, they used dedicated pools + an on-prem connector appliance; we can share an anonymized case study.
[08:40] Sophie Lang: perfect, that helps the internal narrative.
[08:44] Avery Chen: ok i'll summarize next steps. we will: 1) Maya will produce annotated refarch and dataflow by 2027-03-05; 2) Avery to send pricing/marketplace packaging draft by 2027-03-06; 3) BlueHaven to send VPC/firewall rules and sample payloads by 2027-03-08/09; 4) schedule security deep-dive week of 2027-03-15.
[09:05] Ravi Kumar: sounds good. one more micro thing — how do we handle model fallbacks if a higher-tier model exceeds gamma or cost thresholds?
[09:14] Jon Ramos: you can configure routing policies by cost or latency that downgrade automatically to a cheaper compatible model; we log a reason code so app can detect fallback.
[09:22] Ethan Park: ok can we get that config example?
[09:24] Maya Patel: yes will include a YAML snippet in the refarch doc.
[09:28] Marta Silva: and please include what data is retained in logs and for how long — our compliance needs that spelled out.
[09:33] Avery Chen: noted, we'll include retention TTLs and options for reduced logging for compliance.
[09:38] Sophie Lang: thanks everyone, this was great. we'll take the doc and iterate.
[09:44] Avery Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with the links and schedule the security deep-dive; meeting adjourned.

--- End transcript ---
